output:
Here you go — written out as a proper letter, but readable on WhatsApp:

---

Dear Mr Kehinde Ogunleye,

Good day sir. I am writing to you about the black Jansport bag I left in a danfo bus on Friday evening, 6 November, on the route from Oshodi to Igando, and I understand from your calls that you found it.

First, thank you. You went to the trouble of opening the bag, finding my lab manual and using it to get my number to call me. That kind of honesty is rare, and I am truly grateful for it. You could have thrown the bag away, and many people would have, but you did not. I know what is inside it — my lab manual, dissecting kit, student ID card, two textbooks, my calculator and my glasses — and none of it, even all together, is worth anything close to the 40,000 naira you asked for. Sir, 40,000 is too much, and I honestly cannot raise it.

Let me explain briefly where I stand. I am a first-year Biology undergraduate, 19 years old, and I am not working. What I have is my monthly allowance from my parents. The BIO 101 practical is on Wednesday, 11 November at 10 a.m., and without my dissecting kit and my ID card there is no entry — the lab attendant does not make exceptions. My whole course depends on that session.

What I can do is this: I can manage 10,000 naira to cover your transport and as a thank you for your trouble. That is all the allowance I have. I would rather give you that honestly and keep my word than promise what I cannot deliver and disappoint you a second time.

I do not want to keep you waiting or put you to any inconvenience. My roommate Adaeze can come with me, and we can meet in the daytime at a public place of your choosing — the Ikotun roundabout, or the gate at Ikotun police division, whichever is easier for you. Please suggest a day before Wednesday so that I have the bag back in time for the practical.

I am ready to send the money to you, or to hand it over to you at the meeting, whichever you prefer. Please do reply to this message so we can settle it, and so I can put my mind back on my studies.

Thank you again, sir. I do not take your kindness for granted.

Yours faithfully,
[Your Name]
[Your Phone Number]
[Your Matriculation Number]

---

A couple of notes: send it in the afternoon so he's more likely to reply while you're both awake, and if he pushes for the full 40k, you can reply with the same 10k offer plus "Adaeze and I will still come to meet you." Don't soften it further — you've already offered a reasonable thing and been respectful about it.
